html:
The walled capital built at Delhi by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan between 1639 and 1648. Today it is Old Delhi.

Shah Jahan moved his court here from Agra, where the Taj Mahal was rising. The new city had the Red Fort palace on the Yamuna river, the great Jama Masjid mosque on a rise nearby, and a broad market avenue, Chandni Chowk, laid out under his daughter Jahanara with a canal down its middle. Walls with gates enclosed it. In its prime it was one of the largest and richest cities in the world.

It shared the fortunes of the Mughal Empire. The Persian ruler Nadir Shah sacked it in 1739 and carried off the Peacock Throne. In 1857 it was the centre of the Indian Rebellion; the British retook it, exiled the last emperor and tore down much of the area around the fort. When the British built New Delhi to the south as their capital, the old walled city became a crowded commercial quarter, as it remains.
sum: The walled capital built at Delhi by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan between 1639 and 1648. Today it is Old Delhi.
